title: Hamzah's anger
hookLine: his uncle Hamzah hears of an insult to his nephew and declares his Islam (sirah)

cards: A hunter comes home from the desert, his bow over his shoulder. His habit, Ibn Ishaq says, is to walk around the Ka'ba before he goes home and greet the men sitting there.
But today a woman stops him: a freedwoman who lives near Safa, who has just watched something she can't keep to herself.

That morning, Abu Jahl came across the Prophet, peace be upon him, by the hill, insulted him to his face and abused him, and the Prophet said nothing back. The hunter is Hamzah, the Prophet's uncle. Today: Hamzah's anger.

teach.b: Ibn Ishaq says Hamzah was filled with fury. He greeted no one. He walked straight to where Abu Jahl sat among the men of Quraysh, stood over him, and struck him with his bow, hard enough to wound his head.

teach.h: I FOLLOW HIS RELIGION. STRIKE ME BACK.
teach.b: Then he said: will you insult him, when I follow his religion and say what he says? Strike me back, if you can. Men from Abu Jahl's clan stood up to defend him.

teach.h: LEAVE HIM: I INSULTED HIS NEPHEW.
teach.b: Leave Abu Umarah alone, he said, for by God, I insulted his nephew badly. Quraysh understood that the Prophet now had a strong defender, and the sirah notes that some of their harassment eased.
Muslims remember Hamzah as the lion of God, asad Allah; that's where today's line comes from. But notice how he came in: not after long study, but in a burst of loyalty and rage.
Some versions say that afterward he was troubled by what he had said in the heat of the moment, and asked God for guidance until his heart settled.
If so, the anger opened the door, and something quieter walked him through it. The insult was meant to shrink a man who wouldn't answer back. It brought his uncle into the faith.

how: Muslims honor Hamzah ibn Abd al-Muttalib as the Prophet's uncle and a defender of the early community, calling him the lion of God, and his story is told in sirah classes and sermons.

o: the rage that brought the Prophet's uncle into Islam
Abu Jahl's fury at being struck in front of Quraysh
the Prophet's reply when Abu Jahl insulted him

p: the Prophet's uncle, home from hunting

s: Hamzah studied the new faith for a long time before joining
Ibn Ishaq tells it as a sudden moment: anger at an insult, then his declaration.
Abu Jahl told his own clan not to fight Hamzah
he admitted he had insulted Hamzah's nephew badly.
the Prophet answered Abu Jahl's insults that morning
the woman reported that he said nothing back.

games.q: you're Abu Jahl. Hamzah has just struck you and declared his faith. your clansmen stand up to fight. what do you say?
o: leave him: I insulted his nephew badly.
games.why: Ibn Ishaq says Abu Jahl held his clansmen back and admitted he had insulted the Prophet badly.

practice: Think back over the last few weeks: was someone mocked in front of you, at work, in a group chat, at the dinner table, while nobody said anything?
Find that moment, and shape one sentence, calm and clear, that you could have said: not an insult back, just a line that stands next to them. Say it quietly to yourself until it feels like yours.

wordCard.voice: Hamzah's anger. The Prophet's uncle hears his nephew was insulted, strikes Abu Jahl with his bow, and declares that he follows his religion. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the lion of God, the title Muslims give Hamzah.

carryVoice: Your line: the lion comes in. Loyalty came first, and a settled heart came after. Until tomorrow.
